newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes at fresh low, encounters selling.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes at fresh low, encounters selling.

text.p: New selling emerged in the gold market on Tuesday to take the bullion price to fresh recent lows and knock the top of levels achieved on Monday in the other precious metals, dealers said.
Gold was fixed at $338.85 per ounce down from $340.40 on Monday and a close then of $341.05/$341.55.

Gold lost ground in New York and Hong Kong. In New York dealers reported continuing fears of selling from central banks and producers and also cited the lure of other more obviously profitable investments.
Some overseas selling found buyers reluctant in Hong Kong where trading patterns were skewed slightly by Tokyo being closed for a holiday.
"Selling has re-emerged in gold. It looks like a continuation of the big sales we saw recently. It looks pretty horrible," a dealer said.
Some dealers described the development as "quality" selling which usually refers to institutions such as central banks or producers.
Hand-in-hand with the selling has been borrowing of gold on a sufficient scale to double the one month forward rate to over three percent since Monday morning.
"The implication is that it is being borrowed to be sold. Draw your own conclusions," a dealer said.
Technically gold had moved on to swampy ground since it broke through the $340.00 psychological support. A sink to the low $330s was possible to find firm footing.
That would bring the price within touch of the March 1993 low of $326.10 which if breached would take gold back to levels last seen in 1986.
"Further weakness in gold could affect the rest of the (precious) metals quite badly. They are being ignored this morning and have all come off their highest in reaction to gold," a dealer said.
Palladium which reached its highest fix since May last year at $135.00 this morning was about 25 cents off Monday's close.
Platinum was at $353.75/$354.75, up 25 cents but off its high as it spun between support from sister metal palladium and pressure from gold.
"Platinum is at a (near) $15 premium to gold which is unusual in a bear market," one dealer warned.
Silver was drawing breath after its latest bid for $5.00 hit resistance on Monday. It was down a cent down at $4.93/$4.95.
